title: 企業が圧倒的に大きい

candidates.headline: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10
candidates.angle: Invert scale to show private service companies as colossal compared with both the tiny ICC and the comparatively small U.S. attempt to sanction it, highlighting a mismatch of power.
candidates.title: 企業が圧倒的に大きい
candidates.scene: A toy-like tiny ICC courthouse sits on a pedestal; a small U.S. official stands beside it holding an oversized blank 'sanctions' booklet (no text). Dominating the scene are enormous server racks and satellite dishes shaped like skyscrapers; a few corporate figures in suits loom over the servers and casually flick the tiny courthouse like a pebble. Visible objects: miniature courthouse, tiny official with booklet, giant servers/satellites, corporate figures. No words (except previously allowed single-word items in other entries).
candidates.reason: サービス企業を制裁対象にする発想と、実際に影響力を持つ企業の規模差を並べて示し、狙いが力関係に合っていない不一致を風刺する。
candidates.visualTurn: Scale reversal: the companies are depicted as monumental while the ICC and the sanctioning state's action are miniature, turning the expected hierarchy upside down.
candidates.contradiction: Policy treats the court and its accountability as the focal point, but the visual shows the companies who would be hit as the dominant actors—sanctions appear mismatched to real power relations.
candidates.evidence: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10

evaluation.reason: Scale inversion (huge corporate infrastructure vs tiny ICC and small US attempt) is an immediately readable critique of mismatched power. It remains a visual metaphor about relative influence rather than a documented factual claim, so its empirical premise (companies are overwhelmingly dominant in the way drawn) is not established by the article.
unsupportedClaims: 描写が示すほど企業が実際に圧倒的に優位であり、制裁がほとんど効果を持たないという具体的な主張

candidates.headline: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10
candidates.angle: Show the U.S. as the initiator who relies on private service firms to act against the ICC — then flip roles so those same firms are shown being punished, making the accuser into the accused.
candidates.title: 命令者と被命令者が入れ替わる
candidates.scene: Two-panel composition. Left panel: a U.S. official at a podium gestures toward a scaled model of the ICC courthouse on a table while a worried-looking corporate executive stands beside him holding a toolbox. Right panel: the same corporate executive sits in a defendant's dock (a raised platform) with a large judge's gavel looming nearby; the U.S. official is now in the audience watching. Visible objects only: podium, model courthouse, toolbox, dock, gavel; no small inscriptions.
candidates.reason: 米が私企業を制裁の実務に関与させる一方で、その私企業自体が制裁対象になり得るという矛盾を、命令する側と命令される側が入れ替わる図で皮肉る。
candidates.visualTurn: Before/after swap across panels: on the left the firm is recruited to act with state authority; on the right the same firm occupies the position of the punished — accuser and accused exchange places.
candidates.contradiction: Policy relies on private firms as instruments, yet that same policy can make them into victims; authority simultaneously produces vulnerability.
candidates.evidence: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10

evaluation.reason: Two-panel role-reversal makes the irony (accuser⇄accused) explicit and directly tied to the headline's possible tension — but it presumes an operational relationship (US recruits firms) that the article does not state.
unsupportedClaims: 米国が私企業を実務に関与させ、そこに制裁実務を担わせている（『米が私企業を命令して行動させる』という因果）

candidates.headline: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10
candidates.angle: Depict a benign customer-service kiosk that, when opened, reveals a hidden sanctions factory — neutral 'service' transformed into a punitive machine.
candidates.title: 窓口が制裁工場
candidates.scene: Street scene with a single prominent customer-service kiosk whose large front displays the single word SERVICE. A U.S. diplomat stands beside it holding a stack of blank papers. The kiosk's hatch is open and its interior is an industrial stamping line producing small chains and barred cages; a worker inside pulls levers and packages the punitive objects. Visible objects: kiosk with open hatch, stamping machine, chains/cages, diplomat, operator. No other words.
candidates.reason: 外見は中立的な『サービス窓口』だが、その内部が制裁を生産する装置になっているという暴露で、民間業務の軍事化・行政利用の皮肉を示す。
candidates.visualTurn: A friendly service booth reveals its true function: from customer help counter to a factory that manufactures punitive equipment — helper becomes enforcer.
candidates.contradiction: Companies presented as neutral providers are shown literally producing tools of punishment, undermining the notion of impartial service.
candidates.evidence: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10

evaluation.reason: The kiosk→factory reveal is a clear visual exposé of 'neutral service' turned punitive; it maps well to the idea that service firms could be implicated, but it goes further by depicting them as actually producing instruments of punishment, which the article does not claim.
unsupportedClaims: サービスを提供する企業が『制裁を製造・運用する装置』として実際に機能しているという具体的事実

exploredCandidates.title: 正義の秤が傾く

exploredCandidates.reason: ICCを萎縮させる可能性のある包括制裁と、法の守護者であるはずの『正義』像の矛盾を描く。
exploredCandidates.visualTurn: The statue meant to balance and protect the court is actively toppling the courthouse to favor corporate service providers—protector becomes destroyer.
exploredCandidates.contradiction: A government that invokes international law is preparing to weaponize economics to punish the court that enforces it.
exploredCandidates.evidence: ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性

exploredCandidates.headline: 2. トランプ氏、プーチン氏との合意でロシア産ディーゼルを輸入すると発表 - ゼレンスキー大統領は「プーチンへの贈り物」と批判（BBC、AXIOS）2026/10/10

exploredCandidates.title: 贈り物ディーゼル
exploredCandidates.scene: A U.S. fuel pump labelled 'Energy Independence' fills a truck marked 'Made in USA', but the hose visibly runs into a large barrel wrapped in a Russian flag held by Putin; Trump ties a big bow on the barrel and smiles while a small Zelensky figure watches and shakes his head.
exploredCandidates.reason: 対外的強硬姿勢と、相手国産燃料の輸入発表という行為の食い違いを風刺する。
exploredCandidates.visualTurn: The pump that proclaims self-reliance is literally being fed from a Russian barrel—independence becomes import dependence in plain view.
exploredCandidates.contradiction: Tough rhetoric toward a rival is undercut by a public pact to import that rival's diesel fuel.
exploredCandidates.evidence: ロシア産ディーゼルを輸入すると発表 - ゼレンスキー大統領は「プーチンへの贈り物」と批判

exploredCandidates.angle: A political actor announces scrutiny of the central bank's head, exposing tensions between political power and central-bank independence by turning oversight into a political probe.

exploredCandidates.reason: FRBの独立性を保つはずの壁が、政治的な調査で透けて見える構図を示すため。

exploredCandidates.contradiction: A political candidate is initiating scrutiny of an institution meant to be insulated from political pressures.

exploredCandidates.headline: 5. ノーベル平和賞に南アフリカの法学者ナビ・ピレイ氏（NYタイムズ、BBC）2026/10/10
exploredCandidates.angle: The awarding of a peace prize to an international jurist coincides with contemporaneous moves to constrain the court she served, creating a visual paradox between recognition and restriction.
exploredCandidates.title: メダルと鎖
exploredCandidates.scene: Navi Pillay accepts a shining Nobel medal shaped like an olive branch; the medal's front gleams for the audience while its reverse is revealed as a heavy iron shackle labelled 'Sanctions' that dangles toward a small ICC courthouse being fenced off in the background.
exploredCandidates.reason: ICCにかかわった人物への平和賞授与と、同時期に出るICC制裁議論との対比を示すため。
exploredCandidates.visualTurn: The medal shows a peaceful, gleaming face to the public, but its underside is a shackle that physically binds and constrains the court—honor and limitation occupying the same object.
exploredCandidates.contradiction: A jurist is celebrated for defending international justice at the same moment policies are being discussed that would restrict the court she served.
exploredCandidates.evidence: ノーベル平和賞に南アフリカの法学者ナビ・ピレイ氏

evaluations.headline: 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10
evaluations.reason: 強み：見出し自体が『法を守るはずの勢力が、国際刑事裁判所を萎縮させうる経済手段を用いる』という役割と結果の対立を含んでいる。像（正義）が裁判所を壊すという描写は直感的で即読性が高い。弱み：『正義の女神』モチーフは風刺で多用されているため図案としてはやや既視感がある。サーバ群を秤の片側の支えにするなどの細部で差別化が必要。

evaluations.headline: 2. トランプ氏、プーチン氏との合意でロシア産ディーゼルを輸入すると発表 - ゼレンスキー大統領は「プーチンへの贈り物」と批判（BBC、AXIOS）2026/10/10
evaluations.reason: 強み：『自立』を謳う表示（Energy Independence等）とロシア産燃料を結びつける直接的な逆転がわかりやすい。ビジュアルは一読で皮肉が伝わる。弱み：比喩（プレゼントのリボンなど）はやや説明的で、既存の“依存を隠す”メタファーに近い点に留意。ゼレンスキーの批判は見出しにあるが、図に批判者を入れるならサイズ感に注意。

evaluations.headline: 3. トランプ氏、FRB総裁リサ・クックに関する調査を発表（NYタイムズ、AXIOS）2026/10/10
evaluations.reason: 強み：独立性で守られるべき中央銀行が政治的調査によって『透ける』という視覚的転換は明快で、独立と政治介入の矛盾を直接示せる。弱み：『調査』の中身が見出しで不詳なため、図で調査の性格（正当な監督か政治的攻撃か）を断定的に描かないように注意する必要がある（事実を補完してはいけない）。

evaluations.headline: 6. 不正アクセスが世界で急増、9月以降に情報漏洩3億人 攻撃にAIの影（日経、ヤフー）2026/10/10
evaluations.reason: 強み：『支援ツール』としてのAIが攻撃手段になるという逆転は視覚化しやすく、胸を開けるAIアシスタントから攻撃者が溢れ出す像は衝撃的で読みやすい。弱み：見出しは『攻撃にAIの影』と報じるが、『消費者向けの親切なAIアシスタントそのものが直接攻撃を実行している』とする描写はやや飛躍で、見出しがそこまで明言していない。したがって図に使う具体的な“アシスタントUI＝攻撃者の吐き出し口”という前提は未確認のため注意が必要。
unsupportedClaims: 消費者向けの親切なAIアシスタントそのものが直接的に攻撃ベクトルとなっているという明確な事実

evaluations.headline: 5. ノーベル平和賞に南アフリカの法学者ナビ・ピレイ氏（NYタイムズ、BBC）2026/10/10
evaluations.reason: 強み：平和賞という『栄誉』と、同時期にICCの制約が議論されているという文脈を同じ画面で示すと、祝福の対象が同時に制限されるという二面性が強く出る。メダルの表裏（オリーブ枝と鎖）というひねりは一目で読める。弱み：両出来事の因果は見出しに示されておらず、あくまで並列的な対比であることを画面で混同しないよう留意する必要がある（『受賞がICC弱体化の原因』と読み取れる描き方は避ける）。

prompt:
Create a single editorial cartoon for English-speaking newspaper readers.
News headline (source evidence, not lettering): 1. 米、ICCに包括制裁 サービス提供企業も対象の可能性（ロイター、時事、ヤフー）2026/10/10
Satirical angle: Invert scale to show private service companies as colossal compared with both the tiny ICC and the comparatively small U.S. attempt to sanction it, highlighting a mismatch of power.
Scene: A toy-like tiny ICC courthouse sits on a pedestal; a small U.S. official stands beside it holding an oversized blank booklet (no text). Dominating the scene are enormous server racks and satellite dishes shaped like skyscrapers; a few corporate figures in suits loom over the servers and casually flick the tiny courthouse like a pebble. Visible objects: miniature courthouse, tiny official with booklet, giant servers/satellites, corporate figures. No words (except previously allowed single-word items in other entries).
Visual turn to show in the drawing: Scale reversal: the companies are depicted as monumental while the ICC and the sanctioning state's action are miniature, turning the expected hierarchy upside down.
Depict this visible ironic reversal, not a literal reenactment of the reported event or a generic portrait. The turn must read without the title. A metaphor must not assert an unreported action or guilt.
Deliver the illustration alone. The page layout adds its title separately as real text. Do not render any title, subtitle, caption, heading or footer anywhere in this image, including the white margins. Do not write any Japanese characters in the image. Do not add text beneath the figures.
Strongly reference the pen-and-ink editorial cartoon work of Georges Bigot, Charles Wirgman and Charles Keene: observant human caricature, expressive faces and gestures, lively economical contours with deliberate changes in line weight, convincing clothing folds, and sparse hand-drawn hatching. Make these nineteenth-century draughtsmen the primary visual references throughout the drawing.
Create the original artwork for a newspaper illustration that will be printed using letterpress equipment and techniques from 150 years ago, circa 1876. Draw a deliberately composed, human-looking pen-and-ink original for an engraver to turn into a relief printing block. Use economical, clearly separated lines that remain legible when printed at small column size. Deliver the clean original drawing, without simulated aged-paper or printed-ink texture. Specific recognizable characters, expressive caricature, one clear visual joke, spare composition, natural asymmetry, varied purposeful contour lines. Avoid generic AI illustration conventions, glossy perfection, decorative clutter, stock robot imagery unless the joke specifically needs it, and irrelevant objects.
Black ink strokes on pure white paper ONLY. Clear outlines; express every shadow with sparse hatching, cross-hatching or stippled marks. Leave white paper visible between strokes. No gray fills, gradients, smooth shading, color, digital painting, photorealism, artificial paper texture or engraving filter effect. Keep most areas unshaded. Compact square composition, width:height exactly 1:1, complete subjects within the frame.
Design for a small newspaper column only about 64 mm wide. Use one clear visual joke with no more than two main figures and one essential prop. Remove secondary people, inset maps, small labels and ornamental detail. Render NO letters, numbers, symbols that resemble writing, speech bubbles, signs, stamps or pseudo-text anywhere in the image. Ignore ALL label or written-word instructions implicit in the headline, angle and scene except the one specified text element above. Never use fine print or tiny characters. Do NOT draw the Japanese title, a caption, a border, watermark or signature inside the image; the title will be typeset separately outside the artwork. Treat the scene as satire, and do not invent additional factual allegations beyond the supplied headline.
